 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Royal Dutch Shell plc Second Quarter 2017 EURO and GBP Equivalent Dividend Payments </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">THE HAGUE, The Netherlands, September&nbsp;4, 2017/PRNewswire-FirstCall/ &#151; </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The Board of Royal Dutch Shell plc (&#147;RDS&#148;) (NYSE: RDS.A) (NYSE: RDS.B) today announced the pounds sterling and euro equivalent dividend payments in
respect of the second quarter 2017 interim dividend, which was announced on July&nbsp;27, 2017 at US$0.47 per A ordinary share (&#147;A Share&#148;) and B ordinary share (&#147;B Share&#148;). </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Dividends on A Shares will be paid, by default, in euro at the rate of EUR0.3949 per A Share. Holders of A Shares who have validly submitted pounds sterling
currency elections by August&nbsp;25, 2017 will be entitled to a dividend of 36.28p per A Share. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Dividends on B Shares will be paid, by default, in
pounds sterling at the rate of 36.28p per B Share. Holders of B Shares who have validly submitted euro currency elections by August&nbsp;25, 2017 will be entitled to a dividend of EUR0.3949 per B Share. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This dividend will be payable on September&nbsp;18, 2017 to those members whose names were on the Register of Members on August&nbsp;11, 2017. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Taxation - cash dividend</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Cash dividends on A Shares will be
subject to the deduction of Dutch dividend withholding tax at the rate of 15%, which may be reduced in certain circumstances. Based on a policy statement issued by the Dutch Ministry of Finance on April&nbsp;29, 2016 (which has been formalised in
law with effect from January 2017), and depending on their particular circumstances, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-Dutch</FONT> resident shareholders may be entitled to a full or partial refund of Dutch dividend withholding tax. As from 2018,
Dutch and <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-Dutch</FONT> resident shareholders who are exempt from corporate income tax may elect for an exemption from Dutch dividend withholding tax instead of requesting a refund if tax was withheld. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Furthermore, in April 2016, there were changes to the UK taxation of dividends. The dividend tax credit was abolished, and a new tax free dividend allowance
introduced. Dividend income in excess of the allowance is taxable at the following rates: 7.5% within the basic rate band; 32.5% within the higher rate band; and 38.1% on dividend income taxable at the additional rate. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">If you are uncertain as to the tax treatment of any dividends you should consult your own tax advisor. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">CAUTIONARY NOTE</P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The companies in which Royal Dutch Shell plc
directly and indirectly owns investments are separate legal entities. In this announcement &#147;Shell&#148;, &#147;Shell group&#148; and &#147;Royal Dutch Shell&#148; are sometimes used for convenience where references are made to Royal Dutch Shell
plc and its subsidiaries in general. Likewise, the words &#147;we&#148;, &#147;us&#148; and &#147;our&#148; are also used to refer to </P>

<p Style='page-break-before:always'>
<HR  SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">
subsidiaries in general or to those who work for them. These expressions are also used where no useful purpose is served by identifying the particular company or companies.
&#147;Subsidiaries&#148;, &#147;Shell subsidiaries&#148; and &#147;Shell companies&#148; as used in this announcement refer to companies over which Royal Dutch Shell plc either directly or indirectly has control. Entities and unincorporated
arrangements over which Shell has joint control are generally referred to as &#147;joint ventures&#148; and &#147;joint operations&#148; respectively. Entities over which Shell has significant influence but neither control nor joint control are
referred to as &#147;associates&#148;. The term &#147;Shell interest&#148; is used for convenience to indicate the direct and/or indirect ownership interest held by Shell in a venture, partnership or company, after exclusion of all third-party
interest. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This announcement contains forward-looking statements concerning the financial condition, results of operations and businesses of Royal Dutch
Shell. All statements other than statements of historical fact are, or may be deemed to be, forward-looking statements. Forward-looking statements are statements of future expectations that are based on management&#146;s current expectations and
assumptions and involve known and unknown risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results, performance or events to differ materially from those expressed or implied in these statements. Forward-looking statements include, among other
things, statements concerning the potential exposure of Royal Dutch Shell to market risks and statements expressing management&#146;s expectations, beliefs, estimates, forecasts, projections and assumptions. These forward-looking statements are

competition; (g)&nbsp;environmental and physical risks; (h)&nbsp;risks associated with the identification of suitable potential acquisition properties and targets, and successful negotiation and completion of such transactions; (i)&nbsp;the risk of
